stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
For a scheme $T$ locally of finite type over a field $k$, $Z_n(T)$ is the group of locally finite integral linear combinations of integral closed subschemes of Krull dimension $n$, and $\mathrm{CH}_n(T)$ is $Z_n(T)$ modulo rational equivalence generated by principal divisors on integral closed subschemes of dimension $n+1$. If $A\subset T$ has dimension at most $n$, write $[A]_n$ for its cycle of $n$-dimensional components weighted by lengths of the local rings at generic points.

Let $k$ be a field, and let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$. Define exterior product on cycles by $[W]\times[V]=[W\times_k V]_{\dim W+\dim V}$ for integral closed $W\subset X$, $V\subset Y$, extending bilinearly, where $[W\times_kV]$ uses generic-point multiplicities even if this product is reducible or nonreduced.

Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$. For integers $n,m$, the map defined on integral closed cycles by the exterior-product formula above
$\times : \mathrm{CH}_n(X) \otimes_{\mathbf{Z}} \mathrm{CH}_m(Y) \to \mathrm{CH}_{n + m}(X \times_k Y)$
is well defined.
